Actual Article Body:
Florida health officials confirmed one death related to dengue fever on Friday as the state deals with one of the worst outbreaks related to the viral illness.

The Florida Department of Health did not provide any specifics about the person who died in Hillsborough County, but the confirmed death was one of more than 130 locally acquired dengue cases that have been reported so far this year in the county, which contains Tampa.

An elderly Florida woman became the Sunshine State’s first recorded dengue fever death in 2026 after she died from the mosquito-borne disease on her 80th birthday, health officials confirmed Friday.

Gay Small died on Sept. 4 after being bitten near her home on Bayshore Boulevard in Tampa, according to the Tampa Bay Times.

Her death certificate lists “dengue infection” as the official cause of death, along with comorbidities including “septic shock” and “multi-organ failure,” the report said.

“She was in good health and she worked hard to stay healthy and she walked and she ate right and you know, all the things that you’re supposed to do,” Small’s daughter, Anna Small, 55, told NBC affiliate WFLA.

“And you know, this virus just kind of comes out of nowhere. She met the wrong mosquito, and that’s it.”
